extracted.intended_audience: authors (especially self-published/indie) who want to use TikTok/BookTok to find readers and sell books
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, author-focused guidance for creating TikTok/BookTok videos and profiles to grow an audience and sell books. Covers setup, culture, content strategies, posting cadence, and common mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide if TikTok is Right for You
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok is not for everybody. If you're overwhelmed you don't have to be on TikTok — focus on email lists, good covers, and the actual writing instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate your interest in social media and available time; try it if curious but prioritize core author tasks (writing, email list).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stick to the 20% Promotion Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: There's an informal rule that 20% of the content you post should be promotional, and the other 80% should be for engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid spamming followers with book-only posts; create informational, silly, stitched/duetted content for engagement. (Alternate shared rule: 7 non-promotional to 3 promotional.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Save favorite Sounds, Effects, and Videos to Work On Later
rubrics_metrics.description: Save sounds, effects, or whole videos you see so you can reuse them (e.g., stitch later) as inspiration or assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use saved items as a repository of ideas; author reports ~80% of videos created this way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Trends (But Not Too Many)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use trending sounds, effects, and hashtags for inspiration, but avoid chasing trends constantly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jump on a trend if it fits you perfectly; over-chasing trends may hurt organic reach per author experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 3–5 Hashtags (Always include #booktok)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend using only 3 to 5 hashtags per video; the author uses #booktok on every video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstuffing hashtags — according to the author and community experience, too many hashtags may reduce algorithmic pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your Book Cover Is Your Best Friend
rubrics_metrics.description: People on BookTok love beautiful book covers — incorporate your cover into your TikTok marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cover visually in videos to attract attention; visually appealing covers increase engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do a Series of Cover Reveal Videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Create several short videos that slowly reveal your book cover rather than a single reveal video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series increases content volume and hype; use tools like Book Brush to create staged reveals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book Recommendations / Short Reviews as Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Make short videos recommending or reviewing books similar to yours and note your book as a comparable read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to connect with readers who already like books in your niche and to position your work among peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Niche Down
rubrics_metrics.description: Remain exclusive to a specific niche (e.g., genre) to help the algorithm and attract relevant readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your bio clear about your niche; consider creating a second account if you must post unrelated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Other BookTokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Actively like, comment, and follow content from people in BookTok (e.g., those with bookshelves/crowns) to train the algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement helps the algorithm surface relevant content to you and builds relationships with potential readers and collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency is Key (Posting Cadence)
rubrics_metrics.description: When starting out, aim for 2–4 videos per day; if that's too much, commit to at least one per day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular posting trains the algorithm and accelerates follower growth; many successful authors post daily or multiple times a day while growing.

rubrics_metrics.name: TikTok is a Numbers Game
rubrics_metrics.description: You increase your chances of hits by posting a lot — virality often comes from volume and experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat many posts as experiments; sometimes low-effort posts unexpectedly perform best.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoot for 1000 Followers (to unlock bio link)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for 1,000 followers because that milestone allows you to post a link in your bio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make 1,000 a concrete short-term growth goal; it materially improves discoverability of your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Authentic
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity is valued on TikTok — show personality, vulnerability, and have fun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let your true self shine and speak conversationally; authenticity helps build repeat viewers and loyal followers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook Viewers Immediately (first ~3 seconds)
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok videos are short and you need a strong hook in the first few seconds to capture attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-load each video with an attention-grabbing line or visual; the first 3 seconds are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make That First Video! (Start before you're 'ready')
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't wait until you're perfect — post a brief introduction video about who you are and what you write.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality matters less at first; the priority is to experiment with the tools and remove the barrier to entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set Up Your Profile (photo, video, name, username, pronouns, bio, links)
rubrics_metrics.description: Edit profile with a simple face photo (or video), clear name (add 'author' or 'writes'), relevant username, pronouns, a short multi-line bio, and link Instagram/YouTube.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make profile signaling clear so the algorithm and visitors immediately know you're an author and your niche; include nonprofit if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Stitching to Respond and Engage
rubrics_metrics.description: Stitching lets you take a clip from another video and record your response — commonly used by authors/readers to ask and answer questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stitch to create interactive replies that invite conversation; it's a strong BookTok interaction pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Duets for Real-Time Reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Duets let you record yourself reacting to another video alongside it — good for reaction content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duets are less common than stitches in BookTok but effective for real-time reaction formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Bookshelves and Visual Cues as Backdrops
rubrics_metrics.description: Bookshelves are a popular visual cue on BookTok to signal reading/writing values and attract the BookTok audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a bookshelf, use it; if not, you can still create relevant backdrops — visual cues help the algorithm understand your content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural Signifiers (e.g., Crowns) are Optional Signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Items like crowns have emerged as BookTok cultural icons and can be used playfully; they are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such elements if they fit your persona; they can increase relatability without being mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising Opportunities: Promote Videos Only After Organic Success
rubrics_metrics.description: You can promote videos for extra views, but advertising works best if you are already doing well organically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn organic content first; paid promotion amplifies what already resonates rather than fixes poor-performing videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assuming TikTok is only for the young
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok has a broad audience beyond youth — niches exist for many age groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't self-select out based on age; many older creators succeed and find relevant audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake: Most of Your Content is Promotional
rubrics_metrics.description: If everything you post promotes your book, you'll likely struggle to gain engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the 20% promotion rule; focus on entertaining or useful content to build trust first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake: Overstuffing Hashtags
rubrics_metrics.description: Overusing hashtags can decrease algorithmic distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stick to 3–5 thoughtful hashtags, including #booktok, rather than many generic tags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake: Not Sticking to a Niche
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting varied unrelated content confuses the algorithm about who to show your videos to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and stick to a niche; if you need to post unrelated content, consider a separate account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake: Videos That Are Too Long
rubrics_metrics.description: Longer videos typically underperform because attention spans are short; longer videos only suit specific informational formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep most videos short (fast hooks and edits); reserve longer clips for clearly instructional or DIY content that justifies the length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake: Overthinking Videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Paralysis by analysis prevents posting — sometimes quick short posts outperform polished content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When stressed, post simple quick clips with a caption; quantity and experimentation matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake: Underthinking Videos
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting long rambling videos without hooks or interaction fails to engage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lazy posting; put minimal effort into the hook, sound choice, and pacing so the video meets a basic quality standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: End Each Video with a Question or Call to Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite engagement by ending with a question or prompt to comment, which increases views and interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make each post invite conversation (ask for opinions, recommendations, etc.) to boost algorithmic visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Creator Insights to Optimize Post Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use TikTok's creator tools with insights into follower patterns to decide best posting times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check follower usage patterns and test different times to maximize early engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Every Video Like a Short, Disposable Ad
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach each clip as a short, disposable advertisement intended to attract viewers rather than a lasting piece of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This marketing mindset helps maintain consistency, removes perfectionism, and focuses content on discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Trending Sounds/Formats Strategically and Uniquely
rubrics_metrics.description: Use trends in a way that shows your personality and signals what your page is about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt trends to your niche/voice rather than copying exactly; unique takes on trends often perform better.
